opening: I am a very smart student who always pass tests and exams with flying colors. I failed the course. Why?

history.text: Did the student fail because of something they did themselves rather than an external circumstance?
Was the failure caused by another person's action or decision?
Did the student fail despite passing all tests and exams in the course?
Was the failing grade due to missed attendance or excessive absences?
Was there a requirement in the course other than tests and exams (such as a project, paper, or assignment) that the student did not complete?
Was the student falsely accused of cheating or academic dishonesty?
Did the student take the wrong course or the wrong version of the exam (for example, sitting a different course's exam)?
Was the failure caused by an administrative error, such as the student's grades not being recorded correctly?
Did a teacher or professor deliberately give the student a failing grade?
Was the student's grade affected by something the student said or wrote (such as an answer judged offensive or an improper submission)?
Did the student's identity or someone else's identity get confused with the student (such as a mix-up between two students with the same name)?
Was the student physically unable to take the tests or exams (for example, due to illness, injury, or being in the wrong place)?
Is the student a human being?
Did the student fail the course because the course was graded on a curve and the student's high marks were still too low relative to others?
Did the student pass the course's tests and exams but was enrolled in the wrong course or section, so their work counted for a different course?
Was the student officially enrolled in the course they were attending and being tested in?
Was the student's passing work from the tests and exams credited to a course other than the one they were enrolled in?
Was the student enrolled in two courses and their tests/exams were for the other course, leaving the enrolled course with no valid grades?
Did the student fail because the passing tests and exams were not the ones required for the course's final grade (for example, they were practice or for a different level)?
Did the student pass every test and exam, yet the course still had a separate final requirement (such as a final exam) that determined the course grade, which the student failed or missed?
Was the student's failing grade caused by a rule or policy of the school (such as a probation, prerequisite, or eligibility rule) rather than by the student's academic performance?
Is the course taken as part of a degree or program in which the student was not actually a registered student?
Did the student fail because they were given a grade for the course based on another person's performance (for example, a computer system or a partner) rather than their own?
Were the tests and exams the student passed in a different language or medium than the course's required language?
Did the student fail because their passing grades were later invalidated or overturned by another person?
Was the student's name or student ID mistakenly recorded on the tests/exams as a different student?
Did the student knowingly pass the tests and exams by some means that the course later deemed invalid (such as taking them for a different purpose or at a different institution)?
Did the student fail because the student never actually attended or completed the course in question, despite passing tests and exams that belonged to a different course?
Did the student fail because of a mistake in the grades the student submitted or in how the student reported their scores?
Did the student fail because another person's scores were entered under the student's name, so the student received a failing grade instead of their own passing one?
Did the student fail because the course was graded on a pass/fail basis where the student's average, though passing individual exams, fell below a required overall threshold?
Did the student's failing grade result from a decision by someone other than the student and other than the course instructor (such as an administrator or committee)?
Did an administrator or committee fail the student because of a rule the student violated outside of coursework (for example, a disciplinary or legal matter)?

Did the administrator or committee fail the student because the student's enrollment or registration in the course was not valid (for example, the student had not actually registered, or had been deregistered)?
Did the administrator or committee fail the student because of unpaid tuition or fees?

Did the administrator or committee fail the student because the student's exam results were cancelled or declared invalid due to a widespread problem (such as a leaked exam or a marking error affecting the whole class)?
Was the student failed by an administrator or committee because the student was below the minimum age or other eligibility requirement for the course?
Did the administrator or committee fail the student in order to protect the student or others (for example, a safety or welfare concern)?
Did the student fail because the student was taking the course at an institution where they were not permitted to be a student (such as a visiting or exchange status that expired)?
Was the failing grade given because the student's passing exam scores were, by rule, not counted toward the course (for example, exams taken at a different school or as a placement test)?
Did the student's failing grade happen because the student was dead before the course ended?
Did the administrator or committee fail the student because the course itself was not officially approved or recognized (for example, the course was cancelled or the teacher was not accredited)?
Was the student an AI or a computer program rather than a human taking the course?
Did the administrator or committee fail the student because the student's grades from the tests and exams were not recorded or submitted to them by the instructor?
Did the student fail because the student cheated in a way that wasn't detected at the time but was later found out?
Did the administrator or committee fail the student because the student had already completed and passed the course earlier, so this enrollment was a duplicate/repeat?
Was the student's course grade determined by an administrator/committee rather than the instructor because the instructor was unavailable or the grades were handled centrally?
Did the student fail because the course was part of a program that required maintaining a certain overall GPA, and the committee removed/failed them for falling below it?
Did the administrator or committee fail the student because the student was not actually the person who took the tests (identity/impersonation issue)?
Did the student fail because the course was taught in a place or time where the student's passing exams happened before the course actually began (for example, credit earned in advance was rejected)?
Was the decision-maker an AI or automated system (rather than a human administrator) that caused the failing grade?
Did the administrator or committee fail the student because the student was enrolled in too many courses or an overloaded schedule?
Did the student fail because a required prerequisite course had not been completed, so credit for this course was withheld by an administrator/committee?
Did the administrator or committee override the instructor's passing grade and assign a fail?
Did the student fail because the student's passing exam results were for a different academic term than the one enrolled (the exams belonged to another semester/year)?
Did the administrator or committee fail the student because of the student's behavior during the exams (such as disrupting the exam) that was handled as a disciplinary matter?
Did the student fail because another student's failing grade was recorded under the student's name?
Did the administrator or committee fail the student because the student's test and exam answers matched another student's answers (suspected collusion), even though the student didn't cheat?
Was the administrator or committee a court or legal authority rather than a school official?
Did the student fail because the student's passing grades were based on work done by someone else (the student submitted another person's work), and an administrator discovered this?
Did the administrator or committee fail the student because the student's exam scores were invalidated due to a technical problem (such as lost or corrupted exam results)?
Did the student to be graduated receive honor needed pass this class fail, but committee gave fail because student had already been awarded an honorary degree and credit was disallowed?
Is the fact that the student 'always passes tests with flying colors' directly relevant to why this particular course was failed — that is, does the story hinge on the student's pattern of passing?
Did the administrator or committee fail the student because the student's high exam scores revealed an inconsistency (for example, scores too high to be believable, triggering a review)?
Did the student fail due to a decision made by someone with authority over the student (such as a parent or guardian) rather than a school official?
Did an administrator or committee fail the student because the student was not a human but something else? (No—already established the student is human.)
Was the course a physical education or skills course where passing written tests isn't enough, and a committee assessed the student as unable to perform a physical requirement?
Did the administrator or committee fail the student because the student's passing was tied to an external body's decision (such as a board or examining board) that withdrew certification?
Did the student fail because the student's test and exam grades were passing but were for a course with the same name at a different school, and the committee refused transfer credit?
Did the student fail because the student was a prisoner or in a restricted setting where a committee ruled the course could not be credited?
Did the administrator or committee fail the student because the student had a disability or special need that required accommodations the committee refused?
Did the administrator or committee fail the student because of the student's age — for example, the student was considered too old or too young?
Did the administrator or committee fail the student because the student was taking the course for a diploma or degree that was later found not to exist or not to be accredited?

Did the administrator or committee fail the student because the course was part of a competition or contest (such as a scholarship competition) and the student was disqualified by judges rather than graded by a teacher?
Did the administrator or committee fail the student because the student's test and exam passes were obtained at a school that was later shut down or its credentials revoked?
Did the administrator or committee fail the student because the student was overqualified or already held a credential making them ineligible for this course's credit?
Did the administrator or committee fail the student because the student's passing grades were for exams taken as practice or placement (not for credit), which the committee then refused to count?
Did the administrator or committee fail the student because the student was simultaneously enrolled at another school, violating a dual-enrollment rule?
Did the administrator or committee fail the student because the student was taking the course as a joke or for a non-credit audit, so the committee refused to award a pass?
Was the student enrolled in the course under a special status (such as auditing or non-credit) such that the enrolled course could not receive a passing grade?
Did the administrator or committee fail the student because the student had a name or records issue where the committee could not verify the student's identity during the course?
Did the student fail because the committee decided the student's passing grades were earned in a course that was later merged or renamed, creating a mismatch?
Did the administrator or committee fail the student because the student's exam passes were obtained through a distance or online program that the committee did not recognize?
Did the administrator or committee fail the student because the student had not paid a required exam fee or registration fee (distinct from tuition)?
Did the administrator or committee fail the student because the course's grades had to be approved by an external examiner or board, and that body rejected the student's passing grades?

Did the administrator or committee fail the student because the student appeared to have an unfair advantage (such as access to material or a relationship with the instructor) that invalidated the passing grades?
Was the 'course' the student failed a driver's education or licensing course, where a committee (such as a licensing board) can deny a pass despite passing written tests?

Did the administrator or committee fail the student because the student's passing grades had been earned under a different grading scheme (such as a different country's system) that the committee did not accept?

Did the administrator or committee fail the student because the student's passing grades were from exams where the student was given unauthorized help by the instructor (i.e., the instructor improperly assisted)?

Did the administrator or committee fail the student because the student's exam passes were invalidated as part of a cheating scandal involving another person, even though that person wasn't the student?
Did the student fail because the student was a public figure or celebrity whose enrollment was nullified by a committee for publicity or policy reasons?

The student was officially enrolled in the course and passed all its tests and exams. However, they were not allowed to receive a passing grade in that enrolled course because an administrator or committee — not the instructor, and acting on a school policy or eligibility rule rather than on the student's coursework — made the decision that caused the fail. The passing work did not translate into credit for the enrolled course, so despite performing brilliantly, the student received a failing grade.

Did the administrator or committee fail the student because the student was taking the course via a program (such as a foreign exchange, visiting, or transfer program) that the committee ruled could not grant credit toward the student's degree?
Was the decision-maker a teacher or professor after all, rather than an administrator/committee?
Did the teacher or professor give the failing grade because the student violated a course rule unrelated to exam performance (such as using a phone or talking in class)?
Did the teacher or professor give the failing grade because the student did not submit required coursework (like homework or assignments) even though they passed the tests and exams?

Did the teacher or professor give the failing grade because the tests and exams the student passed were not the ones given by that teacher (for example, the student took a different teacher's easier versions)?
Was the failing grade caused by the teacher misunderstanding the student's grade records (e.g., the teacher accidentally recorded or computed the student's grade incorrectly)?

Did the teacher or professor fail the student because the student had previously been the teacher's student in a way that created a conflict (e.g., the student was related to or knew the teacher personally)?

The student was a very smart, high-achieving student who was officially enrolled in the course and passed all of its tests and exams with high marks. The failing grade was not caused by cheating, missed coursework, attendance problems, administrative record errors, or by an administrator/committee overturning the result. Instead, the failure came from a decision by the teacher or professor: the instructor assigned the failing course grade for a reason outside the student's test and exam performance. The student's impressive exam results therefore did not translate into a passing grade in the course, so despite being an excellent student, they failed the course.

revealed_source_answer: The course has a group project which contributes significantly towards the final grades. Unfortunately, everyone in the group except me is a free rider. Due to the huge workload, I completed the project poorly, received a poor grade and thus failed the course.
